audio_seconds_basis: exact wav header value (frames / sample rate), rounded to 9 decimals; the tier manifests record duration to 3 decimals and are cross-checked to that precision (tolerance 1e-3 s)
flight_split_identity_hash_convention: data.splits.split_identity_hash(prefixed('audio2tool', sample_ids)) over audio2tool/<tier>:<id6> -- the value core.flight.FlightRuntime.preflight computes at flight time and an exposure row for a FlightRuntime flight of this roster must carry

literal_loader_replay.finding: tier5_dataset.py::_get_audio_paths appends an audio path ONLY when Path(audio_path).exists(); it has no query_dir/<basename> fallback, and because generation_results.csv exists in every tier-5 query directory the else-branch glob never runs either. Replayed literally against the public release it resolves ZERO audio paths, so _load_query returns None for all 2,146 directories and the released tier-5 loader loads an EMPTY dataset. This builder therefore applies the tier-1/tier-2 spelling of the same walk (identical except for the documented fallback), which is recorded as a deviation in the preregistration rather than silently assumed

official_rule_audit.how_the_file_order_rule_resolved: trivially: each of the 821 query directories ships exactly one recording, mixed.wav, and the manifest carries exactly one row for it with speaker_idx null. 'First successful speaker' therefore selects that file for every directory, and the released manifest and the released loader cannot disagree
official_rule_audit.method: audio_benchmark/datasets/tier8_dataset.py::_load_query names query_dir/'mixed.wav' directly at commit b9d5383ca30945fbafb965a04bea40117e1e8a82; there is no generation_results.csv, no speaker choice and no file-order ambiguity to resolve

population.rule: each tier's released population: for every query_* directory in sorted order, the first recording the released loader resolves. On tiers 2 and 5 that is the shipped speaker with the lowest speaker_idx (the manifest row with the lowest id); on tier 8 it is the single mixed.wav the directory ships, whose manifest row carries speaker_idx null
population.why_not_max_samples: the release orders every subset smart_home -> wearables -> smart_car (its own README), so max_samples 500 over sorted query directories would be a near-pure smart_home sample on tiers 2 and 5; each tier's draw below is uniform over its whole population

selection.algorithm: random.Random(seed).sample(population, count_per_tier) per tier, where population is that tier's official first-recording rows in ascending manifest id order (identical to sorted query-directory order); each tier uses its own freshly seeded generator
selection.rule: uniform without replacement over each tier's whole released population

split_identity_hash_convention: sha256 over the LF-joined sorted 'key' values (audio2tool:<tier>:<id6>, UTF-8, no trailing newline) -- the Audio2Tool probe-receipt integrity convention
